name: Omar Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach bass guitar on Mondays at the music school, play Friday dance-hall sets and record short bass parts for local adverts. I have a music bachelor’s and enough years onstage to keep a band steady, though I still check hard passages with the lead player.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part is good, and what is wearing?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like seeing new dancers find the beat. Waiting for the hall to confirm paid Fridays while a mortgage bill is already dated wears me out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the dance hall that a quicker bookings sheet is welcome. A bass line must stay steady even when the booking sheet gets quicker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have three months of expenses saved, and my partner’s pharmacy hours are fairly regular. One lost dance night would be annoying, not a missed mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep my Monday bass-guitar pupils at the music school and Friday hall sets this season. I would ask the manager for winter dates before promising the children a holiday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the hall calendar, but the household can absorb a single gap. I am not losing sleep over a booking sheet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a party date moved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A party moved last winter and the hall still paid the agreed minimum. I would ask for the same written minimum before the next season.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you like teaching beginners?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a music bachelor’s and can teach a beginner a steady beat. I would rather do that than buy a machine to tell a child where to put a finger.

say: I would tell the hall that **live bass** still helps dancers keep time.
I would ask for the **written minimum fee** again.
think: Our **three-month cushion** and pharmacy pay cover one lost hall night.
A long run of **cancelled Fridays** would still touch the mortgage.
do: Keep **Monday bass pupils** and Friday hall sets this season.
Request **winter dates** and minimum fee before family holiday plans.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about bookings while one gap remains affordable.
S0.quote: A bass line must stay steady even when the booking sheet gets quicker.
fieldNote: His **three-month reserve** and partner’s regular pharmacy hours keep one missed dance date manageable.
He avoids **AI tools** and prefers direct teaching to a machine prompt.

steps.text: Keep Monday music-school bass pupils and Friday dance-hall sets
Delay children’s holiday plan until written winter dates and minimum fee arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the hall that AI may write posters, answer customers and choose backing tracks, and the band needs paid dates in writing. I would ask who decides whether Friday still has live players.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My short bass recordings for small adverts could lose buyers, roughly a fifth of my good-month pay. The hall might try a playlist on quieter Fridays too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would bring the last two hall contracts to the manager and ask for a signed quarter. In the first year, if the hall cuts Fridays, I would ask the music school for an extra paid beginner class only if it has enough working basses, prep time is paid and pickup fits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about my own advert fees, even if the hall stays open. Three months saved buys time to ask for another paid class.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are the school instruments ready for more pupils?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school has old basses, but two need new cables and one needs a safe stand. I would not start a group until the school funds those repairs and checks the stands.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know an extra class pays?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra class has to pay more than the childcare and bus ride after preparation. I would get that in writing before taking a different afternoon.

say: I would ask the hall for a **signed paid quarter**.
I would question a **playlist Friday** before live players lose work.
think: My **advert recordings** may lose around a fifth of good-month pay.
A **hall playlist** could reduce regular paid Fridays.
do: Bring two **hall contracts** to the manager next month.
Take **extra school class** only after funded bass repairs, paid prep, safe stands, pickup and positive written net pay.
feel: I feel **anxious** about advert income and possible Friday cuts.
S1.quote: Three months saved buys time to ask for another paid class.
fieldNote: His own **advert income** could shrink before the hall changes live dates.
The school option requires **funded repairs** and safe stands, paid prep and net earnings after childcare and travel.

steps.text: Keep music-school pupils while obtaining written hall quarter
Take extra class after Friday cuts only with school-funded repairs, safe stands, paid preparation and pickup
Confirm written net class pay after childcare and travel, with pickup workable

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the dance hall that AGI by 2028 may make its adverts and backing tracks, but a paid band still plays for dancers. I would ask for the next Friday run in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my advert recordings to stop in 2028 and think the hall may replace some Fridays before robots can play live around 2031. If both fees fall, the mortgage gets harder even with three months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the manager for a signed Friday schedule and check two nearby schools for posted paid bass-teaching hours. If 2028 AGI cuts my hall sets, I would apply only where my music bachelor’s qualifies, the offered preparation time is paid, pickup works and written net pay after travel replaces lost Fridays; I would keep my current pupils until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious because I expect the adverts to go, and hall work might shrink too. Three months saved gives a short search, not a blank cheque.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no posted school hours appear?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would leave two months of expenses untouched while interviewing. If no school post opens, I would ask the hall for a shorter paid set, not plan around an old advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your partner cover pickup every week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner can do pickup on one early pharmacy day. I would compare the actual school timetable with that day before accepting a post.

say: I would ask for a **signed Friday run** before the next season.
I would defend the **paid live band** despite cheap tracks.
think: My **advert recordings** likely end in 2028 before 2031 stage robots.
The hall may also cut **Friday sets** before a robot plays bass.
do: Ask for a **signed hall schedule** and check posted school hours this week.
Apply for **posted paid bass hours** after 2028 cuts only with degree fit, prep pay, pickup and replacement net pay.
Keep **current pupils** until signed offer, leaving two months of savings untouched.
feel: I feel **anxious** about expected advert loss and possible hall cuts.
S2.quote: Three months saved gives a short search, not a blank cheque.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **2028 desk-fee loss** from the later 2031 robot effect on playing.
A school move needs **posted paid work** and degree fit, paid prep, pickup and written net replacement.

steps.text: Apply for posted bass hours after 2028 set cuts only with qualifying degree, paid preparation/pickup
Accept school offer only if written net pay after travel replaces lost Fridays
Keep current bass pupils until signed offer while protecting two months savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the hall that AGI by 2031 gives us five years to make a live dance night worth paying for. I would ask for a paid lesson partnership with the hall before the show.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think advert recordings end by 2031, but an earlier beginner bass class might replace some fees. Robots around 2034 could play a dance set, though I do not know whether guests would keep dancing to it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This autumn I would offer a six-week beginners-before-the-dance class only if the hall signs the teaching and room fee, eight families prepay, safe loan basses are checked and the class ends before child pickup. In the first year after 2031 I would continue only while eight renew and the fee covers room, instruments and a second tutor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious until the paid places arrive. Five years gives time to test a class, not a guarantee of dancing customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a free room be enough to run the class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The second tutor has to be paid for the hour and for setup. A free room will not pay a second tutor for setup and teaching. If the hall only offers a free room, I would keep Friday sets and my school pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if five families prepay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: With five families I would refund deposits and not book another term. I cannot pay for instrument repairs from the mortgage account.

say: I would ask for a **paid hall class** before dance nights.
I would reject **unpaid group teaching** even with a free room.
think: My **advert recordings** may end by 2031 before 2034 playing robots.
An **eight-family class** could replace fees only if every cost clears.
do: Launch **six-week bass class** only with signed teaching/room fees, eight prepayments, safe funded basses, second-tutor pay and pickup fit.
Renew **paid class** after 2031 only if eight repay and fees cover room, instruments and second tutor.
Refund **deposits** if only five prepay and keep school pupils.
feel: I feel **anxious** until enrollment makes the class pay.
S3.quote: A free room will not pay a second tutor for setup and teaching.
fieldNote: His class needs **eight prepayments** and safe school-funded basses before the six-week launch can happen.
The **second tutor** must be paid for setup and teaching in both terms.

steps.text: Launch hall bass class only with signed fees, eight prepayments, safe funded basses and pickup
Pay second tutor for setup and teaching before starting class
Renew after 2031 only if eight repay and fees cover room, instruments and tutor setup/teaching
Refund five deposits and keep pupils if class cannot run

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to learn music and good work habits. I would still play paid Friday sets if the hall books us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 the before-dance class might replace advert fees if eight families keep coming. Robots around 2039 could play bass, but current school pay and three months saved cover the next few years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I would put part of each paid advert fee into savings after food and mortgage until we reach six months. In the first year after 2036 I would compare hall and school pay, and take a posted paid school role only if both shrink, my degree qualifies, pickup fits and written net pay after travel and childcare improves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feel uneasy about robots farther away, with current work steady enough for now. I would not promise the children a class that has not filled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to saving if advert work ends?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Six months is a target, not what we have. If advert work stops early, I would save from paid lessons only after bills and keep two months of expenses untouched.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children about a paid booking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children to learn the instrument well and get the fee written down. A promise of a full room will not cover a mortgage payment.

say: I would tell my children to **learn and charge** for honest work.
I would keep **paid Friday sets** while the hall books them.
think: A returning **before-dance class** might replace advert fees by 2036.
Possible **2039 robots** do not threaten next year’s signed school hours.
do: Save **paid advert fees** after bills toward six months, then spare lesson fees if adverts stop.
Take **posted paid school role** after 2036 only if incomes shrink, degree and pickup fit, and net travel-childcare pay improves.
Keep **paid Friday sets** while the hall books the band.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about later robots while current household pay holds.
S4.quote: A promise of a full room will not cover a mortgage payment.
fieldNote: His reserve goal uses **paid advert fees** and later spare lessons after bills.
A later move needs **real posted work** and written net gain after travel and childcare.

steps.text: Save advert fees after bills; if adverts stop, save lesson surplus while protecting two months
Take posted paid school role after 2036 only if degree/pickup fit and both incomes shrink
Require improved written net pay after travel and childcare before accepting school role
Keep paid Friday hall sets while booked

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because advert recordings could go before the hall signs Friday dates. A written schedule, paid teaching hours that truly replace lost fees and safe instruments for a small group would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pays the second tutor before children arrive with borrowed basses. A free room is not a fee for the person setting up those instruments.

headlineQuote: A free room is not a fee for the person setting up those instruments.
portrait: At **43**, Omar is an experienced bassist with a music bachelor’s, two children, a mortgage and three months saved.
His partner’s **pharmacy pay** steadies the household, but advert recordings and hall dates remain exposed.
He avoids **AI tools** and asks for written rates, safe instruments and paid setup before a group class.
Across AGI dates he protects **current pupils** and only takes replacement posts with qualified written net pay.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** may erase advert fees before Omar knows whether Friday sets remain paid.
whatWouldHelp: A **written hall schedule**, replacement net teaching pay and safe funded instruments would help Omar plan.
